title: Hanging Herb Planter
subtitle: Convert a standard PET bottle into an airy hanging vertical planter
materials: 1 clean plastic bottle (1L or 2L works best)
Potting soil (approx. 2 cups)
Small herb seedling (mint, basil, or succulents)
2 meters of sturdy natural jute twine or nylon cord
tools: Household craft scissors or utility craft knife
Hole punch or nail/skewer for drainage holes
safetyNotes: Take care when piercing or cutting plastic. Adult supervision recommended when using utility blades or heated skewers. Smooth any sharp cut edges with sandpaper or cover with paper masking tape.

finishedResult.name: Suspended Botanical Planter
finishedResult.description: A stylish, functional hanging planter that saves counter space and provides ideal root aeration and drainage for herbs.

steps.title: Wash and Prepare
steps.instruction: Peel off the paper label and soak in warm soapy water to dissolve adhesive. Rinse the interior thoroughly and allow it to dry completely.
steps.safetyTip: Ensure all sugary or sticky residue is removed to prevent mold.

steps.title: Mark the Cut Line
steps.instruction: Using your marker pen, draw a gentle horizontal cutting line about 10–12 cm from the bottom of the bottle. If you prefer a pocket planter, draw an oval window on one side.
steps.safetyTip: Keep the line even all the way around for a neat rim.

steps.title: Carefully Cut the Plastic
steps.instruction: Puncture the marked line carefully, then use scissors to follow the outline around the perimeter. Trim off any jagged plastic spurs.
steps.safetyTip: Cut away from your body on a firm flat surface.

steps.title: Create Drainage & Suspension Holes
steps.instruction: Make 3 small drainage holes in the bottom base using a nail or skewer. Then punch two opposing holes 1 cm below the top rim for hanging cords.
steps.safetyTip: Keep holes balanced so the planter hangs level.

steps.title: Thread the Hanging Cord
steps.instruction: Cut two equal lengths of twine (approx. 80 cm each). Thread through the rim holes, knotting securely on the inside with a double knot. Gather strings at the top into an overhead loop.
steps.safetyTip: Test the knots with a gentle tug to ensure they hold soil weight.

steps.title: Plant Your Herbs
steps.instruction: Add a few small pebbles at the bottom for drainage, fill 3/4 with potting soil, plant your herb, and water lightly. Hang in a sunny window or balcony.
steps.safetyTip: Place a saucer underneath when watering indoors to catch drips.

title: Self-Watering Sub-Irrigation Planter
subtitle: A capillary-wicking plant pot that keeps indoor plants watered for weeks
materials: 1 plastic bottle (1.5L or 2L clear plastic)
100% cotton yarn, string, or strip of cotton cloth (approx. 25 cm)
Potting mix
Small plant or seeds
Water
tools: Nail or small drill bit (for cap hole)
safetyNotes: Be careful when perforating the plastic cap. Rest the cap on a wooden board rather than holding it in your palm.

finishedResult.name: Sub-Irrigated Self-Watering Pot
finishedResult.description: Utilizes capillary action to draw water up from the lower reservoir directly to plant roots as needed, preventing root rot and underwatering.
benefits: Ideal for desktop succulents and basil

steps.title: Mark the Midpoint
steps.instruction: Clean the bottle. Measure roughly halfway down the bottle (about 12 cm from the top spout) and draw a line encircling the body.
steps.safetyTip: Wipe dry so your pen line doesn't smear.

steps.title: Cut into Two Sections
steps.instruction: Carefully cut along the line to produce two parts: an inverted funnel top section and a cup-like bottom reservoir section.
steps.safetyTip: Smooth cut edges with a quick rub of fine sandpaper.

steps.title: Perforate the Bottle Cap
steps.instruction: Make a 5mm hole through the center of the bottle cap using a drill or heated nail.
steps.safetyTip: Never drill toward your fingers; clamp the cap securely.

steps.title: Insert the Cotton Wick
steps.instruction: Thread your cotton string through the cap hole so that 10 cm dangles into the reservoir, with the remaining 15 cm extending into the top funnel.
steps.safetyTip: Synthetic cords like polyester do not wick water; use 100% cotton.

steps.title: Assemble & Add Soil
steps.instruction: Invert the funnel piece neck-down into the bottom base. Fill with moist potting mix, keeping the cotton wick positioned upright through the center of the soil.
steps.safetyTip: Pack soil gently around the wick without crimping it.

steps.title: Fill Reservoir & Plant
steps.instruction: Lift the top section, fill the bottom reservoir halfway with water, and reseat the funnel. Plant your seedling and watch the wick maintain perfect moisture.
steps.safetyTip: Refill reservoir whenever water drops below 2 cm.

title: Modular Tiered Desk Organizer
subtitle: Organize pens, notebooks, sticky notes, and cables with clean geometric compartments
materials: 1 or 2 clean cardboard shipping boxes or cereal boxes
PVA craft glue, double-sided tape, or hot glue sticks
Kraft paper, newspaper wrapping, or left-over wallpaper for lining
safetyNotes: Always cut against a metal ruler using a sharp blade on a non-slip cutting mat. Cut in multiple light passes rather than forcing a heavy stroke.

finishedResult.name: Architectural Desktop Storage Console
finishedResult.description: A sturdy, bespoke multi-compartment organizer with graduated slot heights tailored for stationery and tech essentials.

steps.title: Disassemble and Flatten
steps.instruction: Carefully separate the glue joints of your cardboard box to lay it flat, inspecting the fluting for structural integrity.
steps.safetyTip: Keep the fluting parallel to the vertical face for maximum strength.

steps.title: Cut Base and Outer Walls
steps.instruction: Measure and cut a base rectangle (20 cm x 15 cm). Cut outer walls: back wall (14 cm high), side walls angled from 14 cm down to 6 cm, and front wall (6 cm high).
steps.safetyTip: Double check right angles with a square edge.

steps.title: Fabricate Internal Dividers
steps.instruction: Cut internal partition walls with interlocking half-slots (comb joints) so they interlock securely without needing bulky brackets.
steps.safetyTip: Slots should match cardboard thickness exactly for a snug fit.

steps.title: Wrap with Decorative Paper (Optional)
steps.instruction: Cover individual panels with plain kraft paper or repurposed newspaper pages using diluted PVA glue for a clean minimalist aesthetic.
steps.safetyTip: Allow paper to dry flat between heavy books to avoid warping.

steps.title: Assemble with Adhesive
steps.instruction: Apply a neat bead of craft glue along all edges, assemble the perimeter around the base, and clamp with binder clips or rubber bands while drying.
steps.safetyTip: Wipe away glue squeeze-out with a damp cloth.

steps.title: Insert Partitions & Fill
steps.instruction: Slide the divider grid into place. Once fully set (approx. 15 minutes), load your pens, phones, cards, and stationery.
steps.safetyTip: Enjoy a clean, clutter-free productivity setup!

title: Minimalist Cable Management Hub
subtitle: Conceal power strips, tangled cords, and bulky chargers in a ventilated neat box
materials: 1 sturdy shoebox or cardboard delivery box with lid
Masking tape or paper washi tape
Power strip & chargers to store
tools: Small circular object (coin or bottle cap) to trace wire ports
safetyNotes: Do not overload the power strip. Ensure cutouts provide ample cross-ventilation so heat does not accumulate inside the box. Never place frayed wires inside.

finishedResult.name: Streamlined Charging Station
finishedResult.description: Hides unsightly cable tangles while keeping phone and tablet charging leads accessible through clean top ports.
benefits: Keeps pet paws away from plugs

steps.title: Size the Power Strip
steps.instruction: Place your multi-outlet power strip inside the box. Mark the position where the main power cord enters one of the narrow ends.
steps.safetyTip: Ensure at least 3 cm clearance around plug bricks.

steps.title: Cut Cord Entry & Exit Ports
steps.instruction: Cut a 2 cm vertical slot or circular hole on the short side for the main wall cord. Trace 4–5 circular holes along the front or lid for individual charging cables.
steps.safetyTip: Always cut into a waste backing piece to protect table surfaces.

steps.title: Cut Ventilation Slits
steps.instruction: Cut several neat 5 mm horizontal ventilation slits along the top rear wall to allow convective airflow and heat dissipation.
steps.safetyTip: Ventilation is essential for charger longevity.

steps.title: Reinforce Port Edges
steps.instruction: Line the perimeter of each hole with paper tape or washi tape to prevent cardboard wear and provide a finished look.
steps.safetyTip: Smooth down edges firmly.

steps.title: Route Cables and Close Lid
steps.instruction: Plug the strip into the wall, thread phone cords out through their designated ports, and place the lid on top. Label each cable if desired.
steps.safetyTip: Keep the top lid flat and free of heavy clutter.

title: Closed Ecosystem Glass Terrarium
subtitle: Create a lush, self-sustaining tropical moss and foliage biome inside a recycled jar
materials: 1 clean clear glass jar with lid (jam, pickle, or coffee jar)
Small gravel or aquarium pebbles (approx. 1/2 cup)
Activated charcoal or crushed barbecue charcoal (1 tablespoon)
Sheet moss or garden moss
Small moisture-loving tropical plant (Fittonia or baby fern)
Peat-free potting soil (approx. 1 cup)
Spray bottle with water
tools: Paper funnel or rolled paper cone
safetyNotes: Inspect the glass jar lip for micro-chips or fractures. Never use damaged glass containers.

finishedResult.name: Microclimate Bio-Terrarium
finishedResult.description: A self-contained water cycle where plant respiration condenses on the glass and trickles back down, requiring watering only once every several months.
benefits: Brings green life to work desks

steps.title: Sanitize and Polish the Glass
steps.instruction: Scrub the jar with hot water and dish soap to remove all food residues. Dry thoroughly with a microfiber cloth so the glass is crystal clear.
steps.safetyTip: Do not use harsh chemical cleaners that could harm delicate moss.

steps.title: Add False Drainage Layer
steps.instruction: Pour a 2 cm layer of small pebbles or gravel into the base. This provides a water catchment basin so plant roots never sit in standing water.
steps.safetyTip: Pour gently to avoid cracking the bottom glass.

steps.title: Add Activated Charcoal Layer
steps.instruction: Sprinkle a thin layer of crushed activated charcoal over the gravel. Charcoal naturally absorbs toxins and prevents anaerobic odors in closed biomes.
steps.safetyTip: Keep charcoal dust away from your eyes.

steps.title: Add Soil Medium
steps.instruction: Use a rolled paper funnel to pour 3–4 cm of well-draining soil, creating gentle contours with higher elevation at the back for visual depth.
steps.safetyTip: Avoid dirtying the inner glass walls.

steps.title: Plant Moss and Miniature Flora
steps.instruction: Using tongs or chopsticks, make a small depression, insert the plant roots, and press down. Tuck fresh green moss pillows around the exposed soil.
steps.safetyTip: Handle delicate roots gently.

steps.title: Mist, Seal, and Position
steps.instruction: Give 3 to 4 gentle spritzes of misted water onto the moss. Wipe any internal moisture streaks, screw the lid on tightly, and place in bright, indirect sunlight.
steps.safetyTip: Avoid direct intense sunlight which can overheat the miniature greenhouse.

title: Rustic Textured Stationery Caddy
subtitle: Transform a discarded metal can into an industrial or boho desk pen holder
materials: 1 clean soup, coffee, or soda can (cleaned, label stripped)
Jute twine, yarn, or fabric scrap
PVA glue or craft glue
tools: Can opener with smooth-edge mechanism (if lid not removed)
Pliers to crimp any internal burrs
safetyNotes: IMPORTANT: Metal edges can be sharp. Use pliers to flatten any interior metal rim spurs, or apply a strip of cloth tape or hot glue over the inner lip before decorating.

finishedResult.name: Artisan Desk Organizer Caddy
finishedResult.description: A durable, weighted desk container that prevents tall scissors, paintbrushes, and markers from tipping over.

steps.title: Clean and Deburr Rim
steps.instruction: Soak in hot soapy water to remove label. Use flat-nose pliers to press down any sharp metal lip left behind by the factory can opener.
steps.safetyTip: Run a cotton pad around the rim; if fibers catch, crimp further.

steps.title: Apply Rim Protection
steps.instruction: Fold a narrow strip of masking tape or hot glue over the top lip to ensure complete tactile safety for daily use.
steps.safetyTip: Ensure total rim smoothness before handing to children.

steps.title: Begin Base Wrap
steps.instruction: Apply a dab of craft glue at the bottom rim, anchor your twine end, and begin wrapping tightly around the can circumference.
steps.safetyTip: Keep tension even as you spin the can.

steps.title: Wrap Toward Rim
steps.instruction: Continue winding cords tightly in neat parallel rows, dotting small spots of glue every four rows to prevent slipping.
steps.safetyTip: Push rows together tightly for zero metal showing through.

steps.title: Secure Top End & Finish
steps.instruction: Once you reach the top edge, tuck the tail under the last loop, add a final drop of glue, and snip excess cleanly.
steps.safetyTip: Let cure for 10 minutes before loading.

title: Window Sill Seed Starter Pots
subtitle: Give plastic-lined takeaway cups a second productive cycle before landfill disposal
materials: 1 or more rinsed takeaway coffee cups
Seed starting soil or compost mix
Vegetable, flower, or herb seeds (tomatoes, peppers, basil)
Pencil to label varieties
tools: Pen or scissors to make drainage holes
safetyNotes: Rinse out all milk residue immediately after use to avoid sour odors or fungal mold growth.

finishedResult.name: Biodegradable Nursery Starting Pot
finishedResult.description: The waterproof polyethylene lining keeps moisture retained during delicate seedling germination without leaking onto window sills.

steps.title: Rinse and Dry Thoroughly
steps.instruction: Wash the cup interior with warm soapy water to clear dairy, sugar, and coffee oils. Allow to air dry in the sun.
steps.safetyTip: Ensure cup is completely fresh and dry.

steps.title: Puncture Drainage Holes
steps.instruction: Turn the cup upside down on a cutting board. Use the tip of a pencil or scissor blade to pierce 3 small drainage holes in the recessed bottom.
steps.safetyTip: Keep hands clear of the puncture zone.

steps.title: Fill with Seedling Mix
steps.instruction: Spoon light seed-starter compost into the cup until it is 2 cm below the top rim. Tap the base lightly on the table to settle soil.
steps.safetyTip: Do not compact soil too tightly; seedlings need fluffy soil.

steps.title: Sow Seeds and Water
steps.instruction: Drop 2 to 3 seeds into the center, cover with 5 mm of fine soil, and water gently with a spray bottle. Write the seed variety and date on the cup side.
steps.safetyTip: Place on a plastic plate or tray to catch drainage.

steps.title: Transplanting Tip
steps.instruction: Once seedlings develop their second set of true leaves, simply slit the paper cup down the side to pop the root ball directly into your garden without root shock.
steps.safetyTip: Dispose of the separated cup in general waste after transplanting.
